items.title: Fired Tesla Manager Says Full Self-Driving Cars Were 'Rolling Hazards'
items.topic: Fired Tesla Manager Says Full Self-Driving Cars Were 'Rolling Hazards'
items.summary: A former Tesla manager has filed a lawsuit alleging that Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) vehicles were 'rolling hazards' during testing. The lawsuit claims that the FSD system frequently failed to recognize traffic lights and stop signs, leading to dangerous situations. This case highlights ongoing safety concerns with Tesla's autonomous driving technology.

items.title: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.topic: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.summary: The researchers at arXiv introduced CommandLM, a multimodal large language model that generates human-readable behavior descriptions for ego vehicles from fused multi-sensor data, achieving CIDEr 0.67 and BERT-F1 0.88 scores. CommandLM processes temporally fused bird's-eye view representations from LiDAR and multi-camera inputs via a Q-Former adapter connected to a quantized, LoRA-fine-tuned large language model. This model is trained on the CommandLM-nuScenes dataset and produces intent-aware, interpretable captions suitable for planner supervision and safety auditing. The strong linguistic and behavioral alignment of CommandLM makes it a valuable tool for autonomous driving systems.

items.title: CARA: Concept-Aware Risk Attention for Interpretable Collision Anticipation
items.topic: CARA: Concept-Aware Risk Attention for Interpretable Collision Anticipation
items.summary: The researchers at arXiv proposed CARA, an intrinsically interpretable spatio-temporal framework for collision anticipation in autonomous driving, which derives domain-grounded risk concepts from accident narratives and aligns them with video frames via vision-language similarity. CARA organizes these concepts into evolving concept trajectories that provide explicit risk evidence, enabling interpretable reasoning about what risk factors are being tracked and how risk evolves over time. This framework addresses the limitations of existing methods, which are often opaque or lack fidelity. By providing a clear understanding of the risk factors, CARA can improve the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems.

items.title: Semantics-guided hierarchical decision-making for autonomous driving via LLM-assisted reinforcement learning
items.topic: Semantics-guided hierarchical decision-making for autonomous driving via LLM-assisted reinforcement learning
items.source: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
items.summary: Wenhao Li, Tao Wang, and Songhua Hu from Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies proposed a semantics-guided hierarchical decision-making framework for autonomous driving via LLM-assisted reinforcement learning. This framework leverages large language models to guide the decision-making process, enabling the autonomous vehicle to make more informed and context-aware decisions. The use of LLMs allows for more effective exploration of the action space and improved handling of complex scenarios. The framework is designed to improve the safety and efficiency of autonomous driving systems, and its performance is evaluated in a simulated environment.
